correctness.rationale: For each anchoring vertex, the two opposite transitive neighborhoods have arc comparisons given exactly by side and the single linear order of index positions, with cross arcs expressed by weak/strict index comparisons. This lifts any winning order game of length q-1 to a winning tournament game of length q. Conversely, rank-(q-1) linear-order sentences relativize to any vertex outneighborhood at tournament rank at most q, establishing an iff. The classical finite-order threshold is \(2^{q-1}-1\), yielding the exact classes, special rank-one case, sharp internal representatives and least distinguishing rank. Modular edge identities were independently checked for m=1..75, and direct Hintikka signatures and arithmetic partitions corroborate bounded samples; finite checks are not used for the infinite implication.

value.rationale: A complete natural model-theoretic invariant for every fixed quantifier rank and an infinite classical tournament family, with an exact one-quantifier shift, sharp representative orders and exact least distinguishing rank. The intrinsic question is how local transitivity constrains global bounded-depth expressivity when no vertex or order is named. The cross-side game strategy is substantive structural content, not a numerical table recomputation; results identify quantitative logical information loss.
